title: The Art of Natural Skincare
author: Nigar Rustamova
tagline: Seventeen professional formulas, and the reasoning behind every one.
summary: A formulation manual that opens with a strict protocol for hygiene, sterilization and safe handling, then works through seventeen formulas, from a pH-balanced foam cleanser and a panthenol barrier cream to copper-peptide serum, whipped body butters and bath salts. Each one lists INCI names, exact grams and percentages, phase-by-phase instructions, target pH, shelf life and a troubleshooting FAQ.
who_for: Beginners: the book states that no prior experience is needed.
Home formulators who want to understand why a formula works, not just follow it.
Anyone considering making products for others, who needs a rigorous safety and hygiene foundation first.
learn: Work to a professional hygiene and sterilization protocol
Build oil-in-water emulsions phase by phase
Set and adjust pH for cleansers, toners, creams and serums
Choose and dose preservatives and antioxidants
Make anhydrous oils, butters, scrubs and bath salts that stay stable

chapters: Introduction: A Journey of Personal Care
The Non-Negotiable Protocol: Safety, Sterility & the Professional Mindset
Detoxifying Himalayan Salt & Mint Body Scrub
Gentle Shower Gel with Physiological pH

why: The author teaches natural formulation and wrote this book so readers could master the craft rather than depend on recipes: each formula explains its choices so you can learn to reason like a formulator.

title: The Art of Personal Soapmaking
author: Nigar Rustamova
tagline: Seven chapters of theory before the first recipe.
summary: A masterclass-style guide to natural cold and hot process soap. It starts with safety and sterility, then covers fragrance and essential oils, the gel phase, natural additives, cure times, infused oils and how to read soap-calculator values. Ten detailed recipes follow, from pure Castile and classic Marseille to layered spice bars, goat milk & honey and a hot process jasmine soap, each with its own FAQ.
who_for: Complete beginners: the book says no prior experience is needed, and it starts with lye safety.
Makers who already soap and want to understand trace, gel phase, superfat and curing.
Experienced soapers ready for the advanced techniques: dual superfatting, layering, milk and hot process.
learn: Handle lye safely and follow a professional protocol
Understand saponification, superfat and water discount
Encourage or prevent the gel phase on purpose
Read soap-calculator values and design oil blends
Work with essential oils, fragrance oils, colorants and additives
Make infused oils and use them as a post-trace superfat

chapters: Introduction: A Journey of Personal Care
The Non-Negotiable Protocol: Safety, Sterility & the Professional Mindset
Fragrances and Colorants for Cold & Hot Process Soap
Cosmetic Properties of Essential Oils in Soapmaking
The Gel Phase in Cold & Hot Process Soapmaking
Natural & Functional Additives for Handmade Soap
Curing Times for Different Soap Formulations
Macerated Oils (Infused Oils) for Soap & Skin Care
Coconut Milk & Orange Soap with Chocolate Embed

why: The book closes with the author's message to every reader: “Do not become dependent on recipes. Learn to understand formulas.”

title: The Big Book of Sweet Dessert Candles
subtitle: For a Delectable, Aromatic & Cozy Home
author: Nigar Rustamova
tagline: Waxes, wicks and temperatures first. Then cakes, cocktails and botanicals.
summary: A practical guide to dessert-inspired candles from natural waxes: cakes, cupcakes, cocktails topped with piped 'whipped cream', and sculpted botanical pillars. It begins with the essentials: coconut, soy and beeswax, container versus mold wax, wick testing, dyes, gel and exact temperatures. Step-by-step projects with gram weights follow, along with fixes for wet spots, uneven tops and tunneling. A closing section covers essential-oil notes, solid and oil perfumes, reed diffusers, car fragrance and a massage candle.
who_for: Makers who want to understand why candles fail, from wet spots to tunneling, and how to fix them.
Anyone curious about home fragrance: perfumes, diffusers and massage candles.
learn: Choose between container and mold wax, and coconut, soy and beeswax
Size and test wicks for a clean, even burn
Color wax correctly with dyes, mica and natural colorants
Prevent and fix wet spots, uneven tops and tunneling

chapters: Why Different Waxes Are Needed for Container and Mold Candles
Uneven Top After Pouring a Candle?
How to Burn a Candle Correctly
How to Attach a Candle Wick to a Jar or Glass
“Sponge Cake with Teddy Bear and Strawberry” Candle
Gel Candle Combined with Coconut Wax
Classification of Essential Oils by Notes
How to Make Perfume with Essential Oils

why: The author draws on her years of candle making and teaching courses on candles and home fragrance. The book shares the techniques she uses so readers can create in their own kitchens with confidence.
